title: CatalystEvent
description: A discrete, timestamped macro event that may drive sector repricing. Decays in relevance over time.

$schema.description: Optional self-reference to this schema file. Present on all event documents (de-facto convention); declared here so strict additionalProperties:false validation passes.

schema_version.description: 1.3 (v11 P2/P3) adds strength_rubric_scores, strength_anchors and halflife_override_reason. 1.2 documents still validate and still score — the new fields are LINTED by catalyx.scorer.catalyst_audit, never required by the scorer, so a pre-1.3 event is reported as a bare cardinal rather than dropped.

event_date.description: When the event OCCURRED (vs detected_at = when registered). Canonical decay anchor used by catalyst_scorer._anchor_date; present on ~all events.

geography.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 or region codes (EU, GLOBAL, APAC, EM)

novelty_score.description: Rubric-derived. Sum of 5 binary questions × 20 each. See scoring_weights.yaml novelty_score_rubric. Never assign directly — compute from novelty_rubric_scores below.

novelty_rubric_scores.description: Answers to the 5 novelty rubric questions (yes=true, no=false). novelty_score = count(true) × 20.

strength_score.description: How hard the event hits. Main sort key. Derive it from strength_rubric_scores below and bracket it with strength_anchors — the bare number is not reproducible across sessions (schema 1.3, v11 P2). Continuous, unlike novelty_score. The SCORER re-spaces it by rank within the registered-event population before use; see scoring_weights.yaml event_strength_calibration.

strength_rubric_scores.description: Answers to the 5 strength rubric questions (yes=true, no=false). Weighted total should land within strength_anchoring.max_rubric_divergence of strength_score. See scoring_weights.yaml strength_score_rubric. Unanswered counts as false — these are OBSERVABLE questions, so 'not checked' and 'no' are the same evidentiary state.

strength_anchors.description: CLAUDE.md rule 3 made mechanical: name one REGISTERED event this one is stronger than and one it is weaker than. strength_score must fall inside that bracket (catalyx.scorer.catalyst_audit enforces it). The bracket is what persists across sessions; the absolute number never did.

stronger_than.description: Registered event id whose strength is a LOWER bound for this one.

weaker_than.description: Registered event id whose strength is an UPPER bound for this one.

halflife_override_reason.description: Required to set decay_halflife_days to anything other than this catalyst_type's value in catalyst_taxonomy.yaml (schema 1.3, v11 P3). The type table is the default and the author picks the TYPE, not the number; an override is allowed but must say why, because six pre-1.3 events silently overrode it — five toward longer persistence, which is the direction that keeps a spent event scoring.

consensus_surprise.description: 0=fully expected, 1=complete surprise. Use 0.1 increments only — avoids false precision.

is_priced_in_estimate.description: Stepped estimate of how much is already in price. Use one of 5 levels only. See scoring_weights.yaml is_priced_in_levels for anchored criteria. Never use intermediate values.

relation_to_structural.description: Relationship of this event to its linked structural catalyst. Determines scoring interaction: confirms → amplification, contradicts → dampening, independent → additive. Required when related_catalyst_ids contains a struct_ ID. See scoring_weights.yaml catalyst_interaction_factors.

sector_impact.description: OPTIONAL, schema 1.4 (v12 B5). Direction of this event on EACH sector that lists it directly in active_catalyst_ids, keyed by sector_id. relation_to_structural answers a different question — how the event relates to a structural THESIS — so a DIRECT event (no structural parent) left the scorer with nothing to read and it assumed every one of them was supportive; the noisy-OR is monotone increasing, so that channel could only RAISE catalyst_alignment (a hawkish Fed pivot filed `independent` added +14.3 of support to gold, copper and EU retail banking, and a `contradicts` with no parent was dropped outright). Absence is REPORTED, never guessed (direct_events_direction_unstated): an unstated direction keeps the pre-1.4 behaviour, so adding the field moved no live score. A relation_to_structural of `contradicts` implies `adverse` when this map is silent.

affected_sectors.description: sector_ids this event hits — CLAUDE.md's answer to 'one catalyst = one driver': a driver may strike several sectors, and this is where that is said. Written since the registry began and only DECLARED at 1.4 (v12 B13); additionalProperties:false had been rejecting 11 of the 19 live documents with nothing in the suite checking.

status_last_reviewed.description: ISO date of the last /catalyx-scan verdict on this event. Declared at 1.4 (v12 B13).

review_log.description: Append-only scan verdicts, newest last. Carries the C2c disconfirming search (`found: false` is a RESULT, never a blank). Declared at 1.4 (v12 B13).

lifecycle_log.description: Append-only status transitions written by catalyst_lifecycle. Declared at 1.4 (v12 B13).

invalidation_reason.description: Why the event was invalidated — nothing is deleted. Declared at 1.4 (v12 B13).

decay_halflife_days.description: Days for relevance to decay to 50%. Default 46 (lambda=0.015). Adjust for policy catalysts (longer) vs data releases (shorter).

related_catalyst_ids.description: IDs of related catalysts (struct_ or cat_). If a struct_ ID is included, relation_to_structural must be set.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry date; null = no fixed expiry (decays instead). Nullable to match all existing event documents.

user_rank.description: User-assigned priority. 1=highest. null=unranked (treated as rank 3, multiplier 1.0).
